children.game_version: A 'musical statues' style game where children must 'faint' when the music changes and wait for a friend to 'wake' them with a high-five.

avoid: Rapid jumping up from the ground
seniors.counts: Keep the 1-2-3 count of the Syrto clear and slow.
seniors.seated_version: Perform the Syrto steps with feet while seated; instead of falling, the leader can lean forward or drop their head to the knees.
seniors.standing_version: Perform the Syrto near a chair for balance; the 'faint' is replaced by a deep bow or sitting down quickly.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduce tempo of the Syrto; limit the range of the 'revival' gestures to avoid overreaching.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Joined in a line or circle during the group phase; used for mimetic gestures of revival by the group during the solo phase.
movement_profile.footwork: Syrto Sta Dio steps (a variation of the 'two-step' common in Greek dance).
movement_profile.formation_and_space: A line or circle that breaks its flow to surround a central fallen figure.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Relaxed during the collapse; engaged for the rapid jump-up.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Includes a transition from floor level (lying down) to a standing jump-up.
movement_profile.partnering: None; communal group interaction with a single leader.
movement_profile.posture: Upright and connected during the Syrto; limp and collapsed during the fainting phase.

signature_moves.description: The leader mimics losing consciousness and falling to the ground to represent a tired bride.
signature_moves.name: The Faint

signature_moves.description: The group uses water or joking slaps to bring the leader back to consciousness.
signature_moves.name: The Revival

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Steady and rhythmic, interrupted by a suspended, timeless feel during the faint.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid actual injury during the fall; the 'slapping' must remain light and joking.

music_profile.meter: Alternates between 2/4 (Syrto Sta Dio) and unmetered free melody
music_profile.musical_form: Binary structure: Rhythmic Syrto section followed by a Free Melody section, repeated 2-3 times.
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Standard Syrto Sta Dio rhythm (long-short-short) followed by rubato/free-form melody.
music_profile.sound_description: The sound is defined by the sudden shift from a steady, driving folk rhythm used for circle dancing to a wandering, improvisational melody that lacks a fixed beat. This creates a suspenseful atmosphere during the leader's 'faint' before the rhythmic pulse returns abruptly.

basic_steps: Begin with the group in a line or circle holding hands.
Execute the Syrto Sta Dio (two-step) pattern in unison.
Leader: On the musical cue (free melody), begin mimetic swaying and collapse to the floor.
Group: Stop dancing and gather around the leader, performing 'revival' gestures (miming splashing water or light slaps).
Leader: On the musical cue (return to rhythm), jump up immediately.
Resume the Syrto Sta Dio steps as a group.
teaching.formation: Circle or line for the group; solo floor work for the leader.
teaching.level_notes: Requires the leader to have good physical control for the 'fainting' fall and the quick jump-up.
teaching.rhythm: Alternates between a structured meter for Syrto and a non-metered free melody.
